newsitem.title: USA: Calif. legislature approves welfare reform measure.
newsitem.headline: Calif. legislature approves welfare reform measure.

text.p: California's legislature on Monday approved compromise welfare reform legislation, clearing a major obstacle for state lawmakers negotiating an end to the state's budget impasse.
Both houses of the state legislature overwhelmingly approved the measure, which would kick new welfare recipients off aid after 18 months and limit current recipients to 24 months of benefits.
Grant levels would be cut and counties would keep 100 percent of the savings. The plan would also provide a safety net for children on aid, lawmakers said.
The Senate approved the measure on a vote of 33-to-5. The Assembly approved it on a vote of 67-to-11.
Gov. Pete Wilson, a Republican, said he was "inclined" to sign the bill.
"It is the first step in reforming a welfare system that for too long trapped people in dependency and denied them the dignity of work," Wilson said in a statement.

Welfare reform has been the major stumbling block for lawmakers negotiating the state's budget for the 1997-1998 fiscal year, which began July 1. The state's constitutional budget deadline was June 15. Lawmakers said the welfare plan would make it easier to finalise the state budget.
Assembly Speaker Cruz Bustamante, a Democrat, told reporters after the welfare bill was passed that he expected lawmakers to vote on the final budget on August 9.
